OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 11, 2026 (11:23 a.m. EST)

STATUS: Direct Diversion Canal discharge, direction, velocity, and strength NOT independently verified. Santee Cooper's operational feed states updated November 11, 2026; its most recent daily lake elevations and facility discharge entries are dated November 10. The daily elevation table does not supply individual gauge observation times or demonstrate matching vertical datums. Do not treat the nominal differences as simultaneous measured hydraulic head.

OPERATOR-REPORTED DAILY LAKE ELEVATIONS (feet; individual reading times unspecified): November 10 Lake Marion 74.29 and Lake Moultrie 74.19; nominal difference 0.10 ft (Marion higher). November 9 Marion 74.30 and Moultrie 74.19; difference 0.11 ft. November 8 Marion 74.26 and Moultrie 74.17; difference 0.09 ft. From November 9 to November 10 Marion fell 0.01 ft, Moultrie remained unchanged, and the nominal difference narrowed 0.01 ft. These operator daily figures are not independently reconciled simultaneous gauge readings. Attempts to retrieve USGS Marion Elloree 02169921 and Moultrie Pinopolis 02172000 via the operator links returned HTTP 403; datum and timestamp comparability therefore remain unverified.

HYDRO OPERATIONS (operator feed updated November 11; tentative schedules): Wednesday November 11 Jefferies Hydro scheduled 3 p.m.–midnight; Thursday November 12 4 p.m.–midnight. St. Stephen Hydro not scheduled either day. November 10 operator facility discharge table reports Jefferies 4,248; St. Stephen 0; Spillway Hydro 8; Spilling 770 (units not independently confirmed here). These facility entries are NOT measured Diversion Canal flow; generation schedules alone do not establish canal current.

INTERPRETATION — INFERENCE ONLY: If both elevations use a common vertical datum and are sufficiently contemporaneous, the reported Marion-higher-than-Moultrie condition is consistent with a possible Marion-to-Moultrie hydraulic gradient. The nominal difference narrowed from 0.11 to 0.10 ft, but no defensible claim of canal current strength or measured direction can be made from these daily numbers. Santee Cooper states that adjusting Moultrie storage and the difference in lake elevations influences canal movement; this describes the system, not a direct current observation. CURRENT CANAL FLOW NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED.
